hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran Military Targets for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The United States conducted new military strikes on Iranian targets on Wednesday, marking the second such operation in three days. A U.S. official confirmed the attacks targeted four one-way attack drones and a drone ground-control station in southern Iran, describing them as defensive measures.

The strikes occur as a fragile cease-fire between the two countries persists into its third month, with ongoing negotiations to formally end the conflict. Both nations remain engaged in diplomatic discussions even as military operations continue, reflecting the delicate balance between armed action and peace efforts.

The latest attacks raise questions about the durability of the current arrangement. U.S. officials have maintained that their forces are responding to immediate threats while talks proceed. The dual approach of conducting strikes alongside negotiations demonstrates the precarious nature of the existing truce.

In separate comments, President Trump addressed the diplomatic situation, stating he feels no political pressure to reach an agreement with Iran. He suggested he could afford to wait out Iranian leadership rather than accept unfavorable terms, dismissing concerns about political consequences related to upcoming elections. Trump also made unverified claims about Iranian government actions, stating that 32,000 people were killed during recent protests, though independent monitoring groups have documented significantly lower figures.

According to Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, the two sides have reached an understanding on main guiding principles during indirect talks held in Geneva this week. Araghchi indicated that Iran could have a draft counterproposal ready within two or three days for senior officials to review, with additional U.S.-Iran negotiations possible within about a week. He emphasized that there is no military solution to Iran's nuclear program, noting that previous attacks on facilities and scientists had not succeeded in halting the program.

Araghchi also addressed uranium enrichment discussions, stating that current negotiations focus on ensuring Iran's nuclear program remains peaceful rather than seeking zero enrichment. A White House official responded by reiterating that the president has been clear Iran cannot have nuclear weapons or the capacity to build them, and cannot enrich uranium.

The intensification of U.S. strikes occurs amid escalating regional tensions. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah has intensified in southern Lebanon, with few Lebanese citizens expressing confidence that any U.S.-Iran agreement would bring peace to their territory.

Iran recently began restoring internet access to its population after 88 days of near-total shutdown. The government had cut connectivity at the conflict's onset, blocking news and communication platforms. Access remains limited and uneven across the country.

cards.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian drone site as negotiations continue
cards.body:
The United States conducted strikes against an Iranian drone launch site, marking the second American military action against Iran in three days. The strikes occurred during ongoing negotiations aimed at ending a three-month conflict between the two nations.

President Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands in the negotiations with Iran. The strikes targeted Iranian military infrastructure as tensions remained elevated in the Strait of Hormuz region.

The military action came during what sources characterized as a fragile ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran. Oil prices increased following the strikes amid concerns about potential disruptions to shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passage for global energy supplies.

Multiple reports indicated the U.S. attacks coincided with Israeli military operations that intensified in southern Lebanon. The strikes represented a continuation of military pressure even as diplomatic talks progressed between American and Iranian negotiators.

The Trump administration showed no indication of altering its negotiating position despite the ongoing military operations. Officials familiar with the discussions said the president expressed indifference to any political pressure related to upcoming midterm elections.

The Strait of Hormuz remained a focal point of concern for international shipping and energy markets. The waterway serves as a transit route for a significant portion of the world's seaborne oil trade, making any military activity in the region consequential for global commerce.

The diplomatic negotiations have continued for three months as both nations work toward a resolution. The latest strikes complicated the ceasefire arrangement that multiple sources described as tenuous and subject to disruption.

Neither the White House nor the Pentagon provided detailed information about the specific targets or the scope of damage inflicted during the strikes. Iranian officials had not issued a formal response to the latest American military action at the time of the reports.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Reach Capital
cards.teaser: Uganda has shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases appeared in Kampala.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases reached the capital, Kampala. Seven confirmed cases of the virus have been reported in the city.

The outbreak in eastern Congo has grown significantly, with authorities reporting over 900 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths. Ugandan officials say the country has strong disease surveillance systems in place to monitor and respond to the outbreak.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: Federal agents found hundreds of gold bars worth $40 million at the home of a former CIA officer.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering approximately 300 gold bars valued at $40 million inside his residence. Federal agents also seized cash and Rolex watches during the search.

Prosecutors accused Rush of stealing the gold bars from the CIA. Investigators said Rush had falsely claimed to be a Navy pilot at some point. The Justice Department filed charges against the former intelligence officer following the discovery of the massive hoard of precious metals and luxury items.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill disaster may be deadliest industrial accident in state history
cards.teaser: A tank rupture at a Longview paper mill has claimed multiple lives, with the governor calling it potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co paper mill in Longview on Tuesday morning, killing at least two people. Nine workers remain missing and are presumed dead, according to the Longview fire department.

White liquor, a highly alkaline chemical used in the paper pulping process, was stored in the ruptured tank. The incident caused severe chemical burns and contaminated part of the Columbia River. Washington's governor described it as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
cards.body:
A federal court has ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address the Trump administration's compliance with refunding tariffs that were illegally imposed. The demand signals new judicial concern about efforts to repay the full $166 billion owed to businesses and importers.

The court's action represents an escalation in oversight of the refund process. The administration has been required to return tariffs collected under trade policies that were later ruled illegal. The $166 billion figure represents the total amount collected from importers before courts invalidated the tariff programs.

The hearing will require the customs chief to explain the status of refunds and detail steps being taken to ensure full compliance with court orders. The directive suggests judges are not satisfied with the pace or completeness of the repayment effort.

The refund obligation stems from tariff policies implemented during the Trump administration that courts subsequently found violated trade law. Importers paid the tariffs under protest, and successful legal challenges established their right to reimbursement.

The $166 billion liability represents one of the largest financial obligations resulting from overturned trade policies in recent history. The funds were collected from businesses across multiple industries that import goods into the United States.

The court's order to compel testimony from the customs chief indicates potential concerns about delays or incomplete refunds. Such hearings are typically ordered when courts believe government agencies may not be fully complying with judicial mandates.

The customs chief will need to provide detailed accounting of how much has been refunded, how much remains outstanding, and what timeline exists for completing the payments. The hearing will also likely address any administrative obstacles preventing full compliance.

The appearance requirement underscores judicial authority to enforce its orders through direct testimony from senior officials. Courts can hold agencies in contempt if they fail to comply with refund mandates or cannot adequately explain delays in implementation.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
cards.body:
Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million on the prediction market platform Polymarket. The engineer allegedly used confidential company information to place profitable bets.

According to the criminal complaint, the engineer risked over $2.7 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The betting activity centered on internal company information about the annual report, which Google traditionally releases to summarize the year's most popular search trends.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions involving a cryptocurrency-based prediction market. Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of real-world events using cryptocurrency. The platform has grown rapidly in recent years, attracting both retail traders and sophisticated investors.

Prosecutors allege the engineer had advance knowledge of the Year in Search results through his position at Google. He allegedly placed bets on Polymarket that would profit if certain search terms or trends appeared in the official report. The complaint suggests he made these trades before the information became public.

The $1.2 million profit came from successful predictions tied to the internal campaign data. The engineer's total wagers exceeded $2.7 million, indicating he placed multiple bets across different potential outcomes. Some of those bets apparently did not pay off, but his overall profit still reached seven figures.

Insider trading laws prohibit using confidential corporate information for personal financial gain. While these cases typically involve traditional stock trading, prosecutors have increasingly applied the laws to newer financial instruments including cryptocurrency markets and prediction platforms.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges. The company maintains internal policies restricting employees from using confidential information for personal benefit. Violations can result in termination and, as this case demonstrates, criminal prosecution.

The engineer faces federal charges that could result in significant prison time if convicted. Insider trading convictions typically carry sentences of several years, along with financial penalties and disgorgement of illegal profits. The case remains in early stages as prosecutors build their evidence.

cards.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times on Wednesday.

Federal prosecutors are examining whether Carroll, 82, committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. The specific focus concerns statements Carroll made under oath about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles.

During the 2022 deposition, Carroll stated she did not accept outside financial backing. However, nearly six months later, before the trial began, her attorneys informed the judge and Trump's legal team that a nonprofit funded by Reid Hoffman, the LinkedIn co-founder, had paid some of her legal fees and expenses.

Trump's lawyers argued that Carroll deliberately concealed Hoffman's financial support, claiming this deception undermined her credibility. Carroll's legal representatives responded that she had never met or spoken with anyone from the nonprofit organization. The judge allowed Trump's attorney, Alina Habba, to question Carroll again in a second deposition.

In 2024, a three-judge federal appeals court panel in New York dismissed Trump's claim that Carroll had lied during her deposition.

Carroll is a longtime advice columnist who claimed in her 2019 book "What Do We Need Men For?" that Trump forced himself upon her in a New York department store dressing room decades ago. Trump has denied her allegations, stating she was "totally lying" and that she was "not my type."

Carroll filed a federal civil lawsuit against Trump for sexual abuse and defamation. A jury found Trump liable on both counts and awarded Carroll five million dollars in damages. A year later, another jury ordered Trump to pay eighty-three million dollars in a separate defamation case. Trump has appealed both judgments.

According to reports, Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has recused himself from the investigation due to his previous role representing Trump in Carroll's civil cases.

The investigation represents the latest in a series of criminal probes launched by Trump's Justice Department into political opponents. Federal prosecutors have investigated former FBI Director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James, and Democratic members of Congress including Adam Schiff and Ilhan Omar. None of these investigations have resulted in convictions.

The Justice Department and Carroll's legal representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing citizens to reconnect with the outside world after a near-total internet blackout that began at the start of the conflict.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access to its population following 88 days of censorship that blocked news and communication platforms. The government imposed the near-total shutdown at the beginning of the conflict with the United States three months ago.

Access remains uneven, with not all Iranians able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the restored access will continue, given the government's demonstrated willingness to impose sweeping communication restrictions.

cards.headline: Record Spring Heat Wave Breaks Temperature Records Across Europe
cards.teaser: An early heat wave has shattered temperature records in multiple European capitals and caused deaths.
cards.body:
An unusually early heat wave is sweeping western Europe, shattering temperature records across multiple countries. London has experienced two consecutive days at 95 degrees Fahrenheit, prompting government warnings. The extreme temperatures have resulted in deaths throughout the region.

Meteorologists attribute the record heat to a combination of a heat dome and climate change. A buckled jet stream is disrupting weather patterns across the continent, while similar atmospheric conditions are creating turbulent weather in California. Residents and officials in five European capitals are implementing measures to manage the unprecedented spring temperatures.

cards.headline: Biden files lawsuit to block release of interview recordings
cards.teaser: The former president sued the Justice Department to prevent the release of audio from interviews conducted by special counsel Robert Hur.
cards.body:
Joe Biden has filed a lawsuit against the Justice Department to prevent the release of audio recordings from his interviews with special counsel Robert Hur. The recordings were made during Hur's investigation into Biden's handling of classified documents.

Biden's legal team is seeking to keep the audio files from becoming public. The case adds to the ongoing dispute over these interview materials from his presidency.

cards.headline: Homeland Security threatens to halt customs processing at sanctuary city airports
cards.teaser: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the department is considering plans to stop processing international flights at airports in sanctuary cities.
cards.body:
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced the Trump administration is developing plans to halt international flight processing at airports in sanctuary cities. The move would be in response to recent protests at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center in New Jersey.

Mullin disclosed the potential action during a Fox News interview, stating the administration is "drawing up plans" to stop processing international arrivals at major airports in cities with sanctuary policies. Los Angeles International Airport and San Francisco International Airport have been identified as potential targets. Halting customs processing would effectively prevent international flights from landing at those airports.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against the US manufacturing giant over contamination from PFAS chemicals at military sites.
cards.body:
Australia has launched its largest ever legal claim, seeking $2 billion in damages from 3M over PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases. The lawsuit targets the manufacturer of firefighting foam used across military installations, with the government seeking to recover costs related to environmental cleanup and remediation efforts.

PFAS chemicals, known as "forever chemicals," persist in the environment without breaking down naturally. The contamination from the foam used at defence sites has prompted the Australian government to pursue the manufacturer for compensation to address the environmental damage across the affected bases.

cards.headline: Snowflake commits $6 billion to Amazon for cloud computing chips
cards.teaser: The data software company announced a major deal with Amazon Web Services focused on chips for artificial intelligence applications.
cards.body:
Snowflake has signed a five-year deal with Amazon to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing capacity for AI chips. The agreement focuses on agentic computing infrastructure to support enterprise customers deploying autonomous AI agents.

Following the announcement and a stronger-than-expected earnings report, Snowflake's stock surged 36 percent. The company also raised its sales outlook, citing robust demand for AI infrastructure. The deal represents a major cloud computing commitment between a software company and a hyperscale provider.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A judge denied Tesla's motion to throw out a civil rights case brought by California state regulators.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

California defeated Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency. The ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, which state officials said they anticipate will begin in July.

The civil rights agency hailed the court decision as a win over the automaker. The lawsuit alleges discriminatory practices at Tesla facilities in California. The case will now move forward to the trial phase after the judge rejected Tesla's legal arguments for dismissal.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided covers unrelated stories (Governor Newsom's tax policy on Trump's fund and UK chalk figure restoration). Since none of it pertains to the Tesla racial discrimination lawsuit, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has petitioned a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed normal judicial procedures by negotiating a settlement directly with the president rather than through the court.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." The former judges are seeking judicial review of how the agreement was reached and the fund's creation.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and Congress to supply Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has achieved success in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The request comes as Ukraine continues to face missile attacks from Russia. Zelensky emphasized the need for advanced air defense systems to protect Ukrainian territory and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Lebanese Expect Prolonged Conflict Despite U.S.-Iran Talks
cards.teaser: Residents of Lebanon say they do not believe diplomatic efforts to end the broader war will bring peace to their country.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that diplomatic negotiations between the United States and Iran will resolve the fighting in their country. As discussions continue, clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon.

The pessimism among Lebanese reflects concerns that any agreement between Washington and Tehran will not address the specific factors fueling conflict on the ground. The escalating violence between Israel and Hezbollah indicates the situation is deteriorating regardless of broader diplomatic developments.

cards.headline: Texas Republicans reconcile with Paxton after contentious primary
cards.teaser: Republican officials are rebuilding relationships with Ken Paxton following his victory in a brutal Senate primary runoff against John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Texas Republicans are moving to repair rifts following a bruising Senate primary runoff. Attorney General Ken Paxton's victory over Senator John Cornyn demonstrated President Trump's enduring sway within the GOP.

Party leaders face fundraising headwinds as they prepare for the general election after the divisive primary contest. The matchup has set major November election pairings, with Democrats now assessing their prospects against Paxton in the Senate race.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces backlash in Italy and abroad
cards.teaser: The Italian automaker's new electric model drew criticism online and skepticism from analysts, sending the stock lower.
cards.body:
Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce model, has divided opinion following its unveiling. The new car prompted criticism on social media and triggered a slump in Ferrari's share price, reflecting investor concerns about the vehicle's market reception.

The electric model comes as Ferrari faces intense pressure from Chinese EV makers. Analysts have questioned whether the luxury automaker's traditional customer base will embrace the shift toward electric vehicles, with the negative reaction extending beyond Italy to international observers skeptical about how the car aligns with the brand's heritage.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe sent back high-resolution photographs of the red planet while traveling to its asteroid destination.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its way to the metallic asteroid Psyche in the outer solar system. The probe captured detailed views of the planet's south pole and other Martian features, producing high-resolution images that revealed the terrain in striking detail.

The Mars flyby served a dual purpose, allowing the spacecraft to use the planet's gravity to adjust its trajectory while collecting scientific imagery. NASA released the photographs, which scientists described as spectacular and unique views of the red planet.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker announced it will begin handing over its new SUV model to customers next month.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has called the vehicle "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 represents a key expansion for Rivian as it moves beyond its initial truck and SUV lineup. The confirmed delivery date marks a significant production milestone for the electric automaker.

cards.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail after domestic violence arrest
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail on Wednesday after being arrested on multiple domestic violence charges. The district attorney has not yet made a decision on formal charges.

Jacobs faces five charges related to the arrest, including felony strangulation according to law enforcement reports. He was taken into custody earlier this week but released as the investigation continues.

The Packers have not issued a statement regarding Jacobs' status with the team. The running back joined Green Bay as a high-profile addition to their offense and has been a key part of their backfield.

Domestic violence arrests in professional sports typically trigger league investigations under personal conduct policies. The NFL has disciplinary protocols that can result in suspensions or other penalties depending on the outcome of criminal proceedings.

Jacobs' release from jail does not indicate the conclusion of the legal process. Prosecutors are still reviewing the case and weighing whether to file formal charges. The district attorney's office has not provided a timeline for when a charging decision will be made.

The arrest raises questions about Jacobs' availability for the upcoming season. Teams often place players on administrative leave or the commissioner's exempt list while legal matters are resolved, though no such action has been announced.

Felony strangulation charges carry serious legal consequences in most jurisdictions and are treated as aggravated forms of assault. The specific circumstances of the alleged incident have not been disclosed by law enforcement.

The investigation remains active as authorities gather evidence and interview witnesses. Jacobs has not made a public statement regarding the arrest or the allegations against him.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell introduce bipartisan college sports reform bill
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have proposed legislation addressing college athletics with provisions for salary caps, transfer limits, and enforcement measures.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college sports. The bill proposes a salary cap for athletes, limits on player transfers, and enhanced enforcement mechanisms for eligibility rules.

The legislation also targets coaching movement between programs. New provisions would restrict coach poaching following high-profile moves like Lane Kiffin's jump to LSU. SEC leaders are reportedly discussing contingency plans as the bill moves through Congress.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses after French Open win in extreme heat
cards.teaser: Czech tennis player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open, saying his body just turned off in the heat.
cards.body:
Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning a gruelling five-set match against Mariano Navone at the French Open. The Czech player described the conditions as "insane," citing over four and a half hours of play in extreme heat and intense sun exposure.

Mensik was offered a wheelchair to return to the locker room after the match. He criticised the lack of adequate cooling time during changeovers, with only one minute to rest. Fellow player Novak Djokovic called on tournament organisers to schedule more matches later in the day during extreme heat conditions.

cards.headline: Spielberg Opposes AI in Creative Filmmaking, Calls for Human Control
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he supports AI for finding solutions to medical issues but opposes its use in the creative process.

Spielberg drew a clear boundary on where he believes AI should not be applied in Hollywood. He stated that AI should never serve as the final authority on creative decisions in film production.

The director did not elaborate on specific examples of AI use in filmmaking or detail what aspects of the creative process he finds most vulnerable to AI intrusion. His comments come as the entertainment industry continues debating the role of artificial intelligence in production, writing, and post-production work.

Spielberg has directed films including Jaws, E.T., Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan over a career spanning more than five decades. His position adds a prominent voice to ongoing discussions about AI's place in creative industries.

The podcast appearance marks one of the director's public statements on emerging technology in filmmaking. Spielberg did not address whether he has encountered AI tools in his own recent projects or specify which applications concern him most.

His distinction between medical and creative applications of AI reflects a broader debate in Hollywood about automation and artistic control. The film industry has seen increasing use of AI in visual effects, script analysis, and marketing, though creative unions have pushed for limits on AI's role in core artistic work.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to criticism over ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: Senator Andy Kim pushed back against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after being criticized for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after the secretary criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin said that Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim said the incident was not about him personally. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement policies and conditions at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and she worried he might have suffered a stroke during the debate.

The CBS interview, set to air on Sunday, captured Biden's reaction to the debate that took place during the 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing and seating
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey officials are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The inquiry was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

Officials are examining whether consumers received accurate information about their purchases, particularly regarding where their seats would be located. The probe addresses complaints from ticket buyers whose actual seating did not match what they were promised.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The classic Nintendo 64 game will join the streaming service's library of retro titles.
cards.body:
Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week, expanding the platform's collection of Nintendo 64 games. The 1999 title will become available to subscribers who pay for the service's expansion tier.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console and featured the barrel-throwing ape in a three-dimensional adventure game. The addition continues Nintendo's strategy of making classic games available through its online subscription platform rather than selling them individually.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kike Hernandez back on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Enrique Hernandez has been diagnosed with a significant oblique tear and returned to the injured list after playing just two games.
cards.body:
Kike Hernandez has been placed back on the injured list with a left oblique tear, just two games after returning from a previous injury. The Dodgers characterized the tear as significant, raising questions about the length of his absence.

The team recalled pitcher Freeland from Triple-A to fill Hernandez's roster spot. Hernandez had an emotional return to the lineup before the injury recurred, and his absence may affect playing time for other infielders including Hyesong Kim.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson discusses coaching change and contract talks
cards.teaser: Lamar Jackson said the coaching change in Baltimore feels like a breath of fresh air and indicated he is moving past discussions about a fully guaranteed contract.
cards.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson spoke about the team's new coaching staff, describing the change as refreshing. He praised new coordinator Declan Doyle for making his job easier and said his love for the Ravens has never wavered despite ongoing contract discussions.

Jackson indicated he wants to leave the conversation about a fully guaranteed contract in the past. He remained quiet about the specifics of his current contract negotiations with the team but expressed optimism about the upcoming season under new leadership.

cards.headline: ABC News Wins Eight Awards at News Emmys, Nat Geo Earns Seven
cards.teaser: ABC World News Tonight won outstanding live news program for the second consecutive year at the annual awards ceremony.
cards.body:
ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins. ABC World News Tonight with David Muir took the top prize for outstanding live news program, marking back-to-back victories for the program.

National Geographic earned seven News Emmys, with Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller contributing significantly to the network's haul. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos used his acceptance speech at the News Emmys to challenge the network's current editorial direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, accepted the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards and criticized CBS News for staining the legacy of the legendary journalist the award honors.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which recognizes student journalists and celebrates Wallace's decades-long career at CBS News, including his work on 60 Minutes. Campos's remarks came amid recent controversy at the network, including veteran 60 Minutes correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's accusations that CBS News penalized her for refusing to compromise factually accurate reporting after her contract was not renewed.

cards.headline: Film Obsession Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie achieved a box office milestone rarely seen in theatrical releases, according to industry reports.
cards.body:
Obsession recorded a box office increase in its second weekend of release, making history with a pattern seldom seen in theatrical distribution. Multiple entertainment outlets reported the film as a breakout summer box office performer.

The Hollywood Reporter and IndieWire noted the achievement is uncommon for films after their opening weekends. Forbes labeled Obsession this summer's breakout box office hit. The film's performance drew comparisons to Sound of Freedom for the rarity of its second-weekend growth pattern.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at National Mall Independence Celebration
cards.teaser: The musician denied his participation in the Freedom 250 concert despite being listed in the official lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall. Despite organizers listing him as a headliner in promotional materials, Day called his participation merely rumors.

The concert is part of a 16-day patriotic fair celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The event features performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed internet backlash over accusations regarding her clothing selections.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed criticism of her recent outfits, stating that she should not be held responsible if someone sexualizes her based on her clothing. Internet commenters had accused the singer of both infantilizing and sexualizing herself through her fashion choices.

Rodrigo made the comments in response to the ongoing debate about her wardrobe selections. The singer did not specify which particular outfits prompted the backlash or provide additional context about the accusations.

Araghchi also addressed uranium enrichment discussions, stating that current negotiations focus on ensuring Iran's nuclear program remains peaceful rather than seeking zero enrichment. A White House official responded by reiterating that the president has been clear Iran cannot have nuclear weapons or the capacity to build them, and cannot enrich uranium.

The intensification of U.S. strikes occurs amid escalating regional tensions. Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah has intensified in southern Lebanon, with few Lebanese citizens expressing confidence that any U.S.-Iran agreement would bring peace to their territory.

Iran recently began restoring internet access to its population after 88 days of near-total shutdown. The government had cut connectivity at the conflict's onset, blocking news and communication platforms. Access remains limited and uneven across the country.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing citizens to reconnect with the outside world after a near-total internet blackout that began at the start of the conflict.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access to its population following 88 days of censorship that blocked news and communication platforms. The government imposed the near-total shutdown at the beginning of the conflict with the United States three months ago.

Access remains uneven, with not all Iranians able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the restored access will continue, given the government's demonstrated willingness to impose sweeping communication restrictions.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Reach Capital
cards.teaser: Uganda has shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases appeared in Kampala.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases reached the capital, Kampala. Seven confirmed cases of the virus have been reported in the city.

The outbreak in eastern Congo has grown significantly, with authorities reporting over 900 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths. Ugandan officials say the country has strong disease surveillance systems in place to monitor and respond to the outbreak.

cards.headline: Lebanese Expect Prolonged Conflict Despite U.S.-Iran Talks
cards.teaser: Residents of Lebanon say they do not believe diplomatic efforts to end the broader war will bring peace to their country.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that diplomatic negotiations between the United States and Iran will resolve the fighting in their country. As discussions continue, clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon.

The pessimism among Lebanese reflects concerns that any agreement between Washington and Tehran will not address the specific factors fueling conflict on the ground. The escalating violence between Israel and Hezbollah indicates the situation is deteriorating regardless of broader diplomatic developments.

cards.headline: Record Spring Heat Wave Breaks Temperature Records Across Europe
cards.teaser: An early heat wave has shattered temperature records in multiple European capitals and caused deaths.
cards.body:
An unusually early heat wave is sweeping western Europe, shattering temperature records across multiple countries. London has experienced two consecutive days at 95 degrees Fahrenheit, prompting government warnings. The extreme temperatures have resulted in deaths throughout the region.

Meteorologists attribute the record heat to a combination of a heat dome and climate change. A buckled jet stream is disrupting weather patterns across the continent, while similar atmospheric conditions are creating turbulent weather in California. Residents and officials in five European capitals are implementing measures to manage the unprecedented spring temperatures.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and she worried he might have suffered a stroke during the debate.

The CBS interview, set to air on Sunday, captured Biden's reaction to the debate that took place during the 2024 presidential campaign.

hero.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian drone site as negotiations continue
hero.body:
The United States conducted strikes against an Iranian drone launch site, marking the second American military action against Iran in three days. The strikes occurred during ongoing negotiations aimed at ending a three-month conflict between the two nations.

President Trump maintained what officials described as maximum demands in the negotiations with Iran. The strikes targeted Iranian military infrastructure as tensions remained elevated in the Strait of Hormuz region.

The military action came during what sources characterized as a fragile ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran. Oil prices increased following the strikes amid concerns about potential disruptions to shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passage for global energy supplies.

Multiple reports indicated the U.S. attacks coincided with Israeli military operations that intensified in southern Lebanon. The strikes represented a continuation of military pressure even as diplomatic talks progressed between American and Iranian negotiators.

The Trump administration showed no indication of altering its negotiating position despite the ongoing military operations. Officials familiar with the discussions said the president expressed indifference to any political pressure related to upcoming midterm elections.

The Strait of Hormuz remained a focal point of concern for international shipping and energy markets. The waterway serves as a transit route for a significant portion of the world's seaborne oil trade, making any military activity in the region consequential for global commerce.

The diplomatic negotiations have continued for three months as both nations work toward a resolution. The latest strikes complicated the ceasefire arrangement that multiple sources described as tenuous and subject to disruption.

Neither the White House nor the Pentagon provided detailed information about the specific targets or the scope of damage inflicted during the strikes. Iranian officials had not issued a formal response to the latest American military action at the time of the reports.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: Federal agents found hundreds of gold bars worth $40 million at the home of a former CIA officer.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering approximately 300 gold bars valued at $40 million inside his residence. Federal agents also seized cash and Rolex watches during the search.

Prosecutors accused Rush of stealing the gold bars from the CIA. Investigators said Rush had falsely claimed to be a Navy pilot at some point. The Justice Department filed charges against the former intelligence officer following the discovery of the massive hoard of precious metals and luxury items.

cards.headline: Biden files lawsuit to block release of interview recordings
cards.teaser: The former president sued the Justice Department to prevent the release of audio from interviews conducted by special counsel Robert Hur.
cards.body:
Joe Biden has filed a lawsuit against the Justice Department to prevent the release of audio recordings from his interviews with special counsel Robert Hur. The recordings were made during Hur's investigation into Biden's handling of classified documents.

Biden's legal team is seeking to keep the audio files from becoming public. The case adds to the ongoing dispute over these interview materials from his presidency.

cards.headline: Homeland Security threatens to halt customs processing at sanctuary city airports
cards.teaser: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the department is considering plans to stop processing international flights at airports in sanctuary cities.
cards.body:
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced the Trump administration is developing plans to halt international flight processing at airports in sanctuary cities. The move would be in response to recent protests at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center in New Jersey.

Mullin disclosed the potential action during a Fox News interview, stating the administration is "drawing up plans" to stop processing international arrivals at major airports in cities with sanctuary policies. Los Angeles International Airport and San Francisco International Airport have been identified as potential targets. Halting customs processing would effectively prevent international flights from landing at those airports.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill disaster may be deadliest industrial accident in state history
cards.teaser: A tank rupture at a Longview paper mill has claimed multiple lives, with the governor calling it potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co paper mill in Longview on Tuesday morning, killing at least two people. Nine workers remain missing and are presumed dead, according to the Longview fire department.

White liquor, a highly alkaline chemical used in the paper pulping process, was stored in the ruptured tank. The incident caused severe chemical burns and contaminated part of the Columbia River. Washington's governor described it as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history.

cards.headline: Texas Republicans reconcile with Paxton after contentious primary
cards.teaser: Republican officials are rebuilding relationships with Ken Paxton following his victory in a brutal Senate primary runoff against John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Texas Republicans are moving to repair rifts following a bruising Senate primary runoff. Attorney General Ken Paxton's victory over Senator John Cornyn demonstrated President Trump's enduring sway within the GOP.

Party leaders face fundraising headwinds as they prepare for the general election after the divisive primary contest. The matchup has set major November election pairings, with Democrats now assessing their prospects against Paxton in the Senate race.

hero.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
hero.body:
A federal court has ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address the Trump administration's compliance with refunding tariffs that were illegally imposed. The demand signals new judicial concern about efforts to repay the full $166 billion owed to businesses and importers.

The court's action represents an escalation in oversight of the refund process. The administration has been required to return tariffs collected under trade policies that were later ruled illegal. The $166 billion figure represents the total amount collected from importers before courts invalidated the tariff programs.

The hearing will require the customs chief to explain the status of refunds and detail steps being taken to ensure full compliance with court orders. The directive suggests judges are not satisfied with the pace or completeness of the repayment effort.

The refund obligation stems from tariff policies implemented during the Trump administration that courts subsequently found violated trade law. Importers paid the tariffs under protest, and successful legal challenges established their right to reimbursement.

The $166 billion liability represents one of the largest financial obligations resulting from overturned trade policies in recent history. The funds were collected from businesses across multiple industries that import goods into the United States.

The court's order to compel testimony from the customs chief indicates potential concerns about delays or incomplete refunds. Such hearings are typically ordered when courts believe government agencies may not be fully complying with judicial mandates.

The customs chief will need to provide detailed accounting of how much has been refunded, how much remains outstanding, and what timeline exists for completing the payments. The hearing will also likely address any administrative obstacles preventing full compliance.

The appearance requirement underscores judicial authority to enforce its orders through direct testimony from senior officials. Courts can hold agencies in contempt if they fail to comply with refund mandates or cannot adequately explain delays in implementation.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a lawsuit against the US manufacturing giant over contamination from PFAS chemicals at military sites.
cards.body:
Australia has launched its largest ever legal claim, seeking $2 billion in damages from 3M over PFAS contamination at 28 defence bases. The lawsuit targets the manufacturer of firefighting foam used across military installations, with the government seeking to recover costs related to environmental cleanup and remediation efforts.

PFAS chemicals, known as "forever chemicals," persist in the environment without breaking down naturally. The contamination from the foam used at defence sites has prompted the Australian government to pursue the manufacturer for compensation to address the environmental damage across the affected bases.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading after $1.2 million in bets
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a longtime Google worker with using internal company data to place bets on Polymarket.
cards.body:
Michele Spagnuolo, a longtime Google engineer, has been charged with insider trading after allegedly using confidential company information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets. According to federal prosecutors, Spagnuolo accessed Google's internal data about search trends related to the company's 2025 Year in Search campaign before placing wagers on Polymarket, a prediction market platform.

The case marks an unusual application of insider trading laws to prediction markets. Prosecutors allege Spagnuolo knew the outcomes of his bets before the general public because he had access to Google's confidential information. The charges were filed in New York, where Spagnuolo worked for Google.

cards.headline: Snowflake commits $6 billion to Amazon for cloud computing chips
cards.teaser: The data software company announced a major deal with Amazon Web Services focused on chips for artificial intelligence applications.
cards.body:
Snowflake has signed a five-year deal with Amazon to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing capacity for AI chips. The agreement focuses on agentic computing infrastructure to support enterprise customers deploying autonomous AI agents.

Following the announcement and a stronger-than-expected earnings report, Snowflake's stock surged 36 percent. The company also raised its sales outlook, citing robust demand for AI infrastructure. The deal represents a major cloud computing commitment between a software company and a hyperscale provider.

cards.headline: Ferrari's first electric car faces backlash in Italy and abroad
cards.teaser: The Italian automaker's new electric model drew criticism online and skepticism from analysts, sending the stock lower.
cards.body:
Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce model, has divided opinion following its unveiling. The new car prompted criticism on social media and triggered a slump in Ferrari's share price, reflecting investor concerns about the vehicle's market reception.

The electric model comes as Ferrari faces intense pressure from Chinese EV makers. Analysts have questioned whether the luxury automaker's traditional customer base will embrace the shift toward electric vehicles, with the negative reaction extending beyond Italy to international observers skeptical about how the car aligns with the brand's heritage.

cards.headline: FIFA under investigation over World Cup ticket pricing and seating
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey officials are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The inquiry was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

Officials are examining whether consumers received accurate information about their purchases, particularly regarding where their seats would be located. The probe addresses complaints from ticket buyers whose actual seating did not match what they were promised.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
hero.body:
Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million on the prediction market platform Polymarket. The engineer allegedly used confidential company information to place profitable bets.

According to the criminal complaint, the engineer risked over $2.7 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The betting activity centered on internal company information about the annual report, which Google traditionally releases to summarize the year's most popular search trends.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions involving a cryptocurrency-based prediction market. Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of real-world events using cryptocurrency. The platform has grown rapidly in recent years, attracting both retail traders and sophisticated investors.

Prosecutors allege the engineer had advance knowledge of the Year in Search results through his position at Google. He allegedly placed bets on Polymarket that would profit if certain search terms or trends appeared in the official report. The complaint suggests he made these trades before the information became public.

The $1.2 million profit came from successful predictions tied to the internal campaign data. The engineer's total wagers exceeded $2.7 million, indicating he placed multiple bets across different potential outcomes. Some of those bets apparently did not pay off, but his overall profit still reached seven figures.

Insider trading laws prohibit using confidential corporate information for personal financial gain. While these cases typically involve traditional stock trading, prosecutors have increasingly applied the laws to newer financial instruments including cryptocurrency markets and prediction platforms.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges. The company maintains internal policies restricting employees from using confidential information for personal benefit. Violations can result in termination and, as this case demonstrates, criminal prosecution.

The engineer faces federal charges that could result in significant prison time if convicted. Insider trading convictions typically carry sentences of several years, along with financial penalties and disgorgement of illegal profits. The case remains in early stages as prosecutors build their evidence.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A judge denied Tesla's motion to throw out a civil rights case brought by California state regulators.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

California defeated Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency. The ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, which state officials said they anticipate will begin in July.

The civil rights agency hailed the court decision as a win over the automaker. The lawsuit alleges discriminatory practices at Tesla facilities in California. The case will now move forward to the trial phase after the judge rejected Tesla's legal arguments for dismissal.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided covers unrelated stories (Governor Newsom's tax policy on Trump's fund and UK chalk figure restoration). Since none of it pertains to the Tesla racial discrimination lawsuit, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe sent back high-resolution photographs of the red planet while traveling to its asteroid destination.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its way to the metallic asteroid Psyche in the outer solar system. The probe captured detailed views of the planet's south pole and other Martian features, producing high-resolution images that revealed the terrain in striking detail.

The Mars flyby served a dual purpose, allowing the spacecraft to use the planet's gravity to adjust its trajectory while collecting scientific imagery. NASA released the photographs, which scientists described as spectacular and unique views of the red planet.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker announced it will begin handing over its new SUV model to customers next month.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has called the vehicle "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 represents a key expansion for Rivian as it moves beyond its initial truck and SUV lineup. The confirmed delivery date marks a significant production milestone for the electric automaker.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The classic Nintendo 64 game will join the streaming service's library of retro titles.
cards.body:
Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week, expanding the platform's collection of Nintendo 64 games. The 1999 title will become available to subscribers who pay for the service's expansion tier.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console and featured the barrel-throwing ape in a three-dimensional adventure game. The addition continues Nintendo's strategy of making classic games available through its online subscription platform rather than selling them individually.

hero.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs released from jail after domestic violence arrest
hero.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail on Wednesday after being arrested on multiple domestic violence charges. The district attorney has not yet made a decision on formal charges.

Jacobs faces five charges related to the arrest, including felony strangulation according to law enforcement reports. He was taken into custody earlier this week but released as the investigation continues.

The Packers have not issued a statement regarding Jacobs' status with the team. The running back joined Green Bay as a high-profile addition to their offense and has been a key part of their backfield.

Domestic violence arrests in professional sports typically trigger league investigations under personal conduct policies. The NFL has disciplinary protocols that can result in suspensions or other penalties depending on the outcome of criminal proceedings.

Jacobs' release from jail does not indicate the conclusion of the legal process. Prosecutors are still reviewing the case and weighing whether to file formal charges. The district attorney's office has not provided a timeline for when a charging decision will be made.

The arrest raises questions about Jacobs' availability for the upcoming season. Teams often place players on administrative leave or the commissioner's exempt list while legal matters are resolved, though no such action has been announced.

Felony strangulation charges carry serious legal consequences in most jurisdictions and are treated as aggravated forms of assault. The specific circumstances of the alleged incident have not been disclosed by law enforcement.

The investigation remains active as authorities gather evidence and interview witnesses. Jacobs has not made a public statement regarding the arrest or the allegations against him.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell introduce bipartisan college sports reform bill
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have proposed legislation addressing college athletics with provisions for salary caps, transfer limits, and enforcement measures.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college sports. The bill proposes a salary cap for athletes, limits on player transfers, and enhanced enforcement mechanisms for eligibility rules.

The legislation also targets coaching movement between programs. New provisions would restrict coach poaching following high-profile moves like Lane Kiffin's jump to LSU. SEC leaders are reportedly discussing contingency plans as the bill moves through Congress.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Kike Hernandez back on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Enrique Hernandez has been diagnosed with a significant oblique tear and returned to the injured list after playing just two games.
cards.body:
Kike Hernandez has been placed back on the injured list with a left oblique tear, just two games after returning from a previous injury. The Dodgers characterized the tear as significant, raising questions about the length of his absence.

The team recalled pitcher Freeland from Triple-A to fill Hernandez's roster spot. Hernandez had an emotional return to the lineup before the injury recurred, and his absence may affect playing time for other infielders including Hyesong Kim.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson discusses coaching change and contract talks
cards.teaser: Lamar Jackson said the coaching change in Baltimore feels like a breath of fresh air and indicated he is moving past discussions about a fully guaranteed contract.
cards.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson spoke about the team's new coaching staff, describing the change as refreshing. He praised new coordinator Declan Doyle for making his job easier and said his love for the Ravens has never wavered despite ongoing contract discussions.

Jackson indicated he wants to leave the conversation about a fully guaranteed contract in the past. He remained quiet about the specifics of his current contract negotiations with the team but expressed optimism about the upcoming season under new leadership.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses after French Open win in extreme heat
cards.teaser: Czech tennis player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open, saying his body just turned off in the heat.
cards.body:
Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning a gruelling five-set match against Mariano Navone at the French Open. The Czech player described the conditions as "insane," citing over four and a half hours of play in extreme heat and intense sun exposure.

Mensik was offered a wheelchair to return to the locker room after the match. He criticised the lack of adequate cooling time during changeovers, with only one minute to rest. Fellow player Novak Djokovic called on tournament organisers to schedule more matches later in the day during extreme heat conditions.

hero.headline: Spielberg Opposes AI in Creative Filmmaking, Calls for Human Control
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in creative filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he supports AI for finding solutions to medical issues but opposes its use in the creative process.

Spielberg drew a clear boundary on where he believes AI should not be applied in Hollywood. He stated that AI should never serve as the final authority on creative decisions in film production.

The director did not elaborate on specific examples of AI use in filmmaking or detail what aspects of the creative process he finds most vulnerable to AI intrusion. His comments come as the entertainment industry continues debating the role of artificial intelligence in production, writing, and post-production work.

Spielberg has directed films including Jaws, E.T., Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan over a career spanning more than five decades. His position adds a prominent voice to ongoing discussions about AI's place in creative industries.

The podcast appearance marks one of the director's public statements on emerging technology in filmmaking. Spielberg did not address whether he has encountered AI tools in his own recent projects or specify which applications concern him most.

His distinction between medical and creative applications of AI reflects a broader debate in Hollywood about automation and artistic control. The film industry has seen increasing use of AI in visual effects, script analysis, and marketing, though creative unions have pushed for limits on AI's role in core artistic work.

cards.headline: ABC News Wins Eight Awards at News Emmys, Nat Geo Earns Seven
cards.teaser: ABC World News Tonight won outstanding live news program for the second consecutive year at the annual awards ceremony.
cards.body:
ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins. ABC World News Tonight with David Muir took the top prize for outstanding live news program, marking back-to-back victories for the program.

National Geographic earned seven News Emmys, with Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller contributing significantly to the network's haul. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos used his acceptance speech at the News Emmys to challenge the network's current editorial direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, accepted the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards and criticized CBS News for staining the legacy of the legendary journalist the award honors.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which recognizes student journalists and celebrates Wallace's decades-long career at CBS News, including his work on 60 Minutes. Campos's remarks came amid recent controversy at the network, including veteran 60 Minutes correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's accusations that CBS News penalized her for refusing to compromise factually accurate reporting after her contract was not renewed.

cards.headline: Film Obsession Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie achieved a box office milestone rarely seen in theatrical releases, according to industry reports.
cards.body:
Obsession recorded a box office increase in its second weekend of release, making history with a pattern seldom seen in theatrical distribution. Multiple entertainment outlets reported the film as a breakout summer box office performer.

The Hollywood Reporter and IndieWire noted the achievement is uncommon for films after their opening weekends. Forbes labeled Obsession this summer's breakout box office hit. The film's performance drew comparisons to Sound of Freedom for the rarity of its second-weekend growth pattern.

cards.headline: Morris Day Says He Will Not Perform at National Mall Independence Celebration
cards.teaser: The musician denied his participation in the Freedom 250 concert despite being listed in the official lineup.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall. Despite organizers listing him as a headliner in promotional materials, Day called his participation merely rumors.

The concert is part of a 16-day patriotic fair celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The event features performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: The singer addressed internet backlash over accusations regarding her clothing selections.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed criticism of her recent outfits, stating that she should not be held responsible if someone sexualizes her based on her clothing. Internet commenters had accused the singer of both infantilizing and sexualizing herself through her fashion choices.

Rodrigo made the comments in response to the ongoing debate about her wardrobe selections. The singer did not specify which particular outfits prompted the backlash or provide additional context about the accusations.

hero.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times on Wednesday.

Federal prosecutors are examining whether Carroll, 82, committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. The specific focus concerns statements Carroll made under oath about whether she received outside financial support for her legal battles.

During the 2022 deposition, Carroll stated she did not accept outside financial backing. However, nearly six months later, before the trial began, her attorneys informed the judge and Trump's legal team that a nonprofit funded by Reid Hoffman, the LinkedIn co-founder, had paid some of her legal fees and expenses.

Trump's lawyers argued that Carroll deliberately concealed Hoffman's financial support, claiming this deception undermined her credibility. Carroll's legal representatives responded that she had never met or spoken with anyone from the nonprofit organization. The judge allowed Trump's attorney, Alina Habba, to question Carroll again in a second deposition.

In 2024, a three-judge federal appeals court panel in New York dismissed Trump's claim that Carroll had lied during her deposition.

Carroll is a longtime advice columnist who claimed in her 2019 book "What Do We Need Men For?" that Trump forced himself upon her in a New York department store dressing room decades ago. Trump has denied her allegations, stating she was "totally lying" and that she was "not my type."

Carroll filed a federal civil lawsuit against Trump for sexual abuse and defamation. A jury found Trump liable on both counts and awarded Carroll five million dollars in damages. A year later, another jury ordered Trump to pay eighty-three million dollars in a separate defamation case. Trump has appealed both judgments.

According to reports, Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has recused himself from the investigation due to his previous role representing Trump in Carroll's civil cases.

The investigation represents the latest in a series of criminal probes launched by Trump's Justice Department into political opponents. Federal prosecutors have investigated former FBI Director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James, and Democratic members of Congress including Adam Schiff and Ilhan Omar. None of these investigations have resulted in convictions.

The Justice Department and Carroll's legal representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has petitioned a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed normal judicial procedures by negotiating a settlement directly with the president rather than through the court.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." The former judges are seeking judicial review of how the agreement was reached and the fund's creation.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to criticism over ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: Senator Andy Kim pushed back against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after being criticized for attending a protest at a migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after the secretary criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. During a Cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin said that Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim said the incident was not about him personally. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement policies and conditions at detention facilities.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and Congress to supply Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked President Trump and members of Congress to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia. Zelensky said Ukraine has achieved success in defending against drones but has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The request comes as Ukraine continues to face missile attacks from Russia. Zelensky emphasized the need for advanced air defense systems to protect Ukrainian territory and infrastructure.
